stances_toward.note: Claimed, not controlled: Russian forces hold South Ossetia since the August 2008 war, with 'borderisation' fences moving the line (RUSI cites the 2015 Tsitelubani markers affecting the Baku-Supsa pipeline). The Georgian parliament abolished the Temporary Administration of South Ossetia on 17 December 2025, which Jamestown reads as meeting a Russian demand. Bond grievance: the 2008 war.

stances_toward.note: Recognised by decree No. 1261 on 26 Aug 2008; the 2015 Treaty on Alliance and Integration (18 Mar 2015) and the Treaty on the Deepening of Allied Interaction signed by Putin and Gagloev on 9 May 2026 and ratified by federal law 136-FZ (25 May 2026), which Tbilisi calls a further step to annexation and JAMnews 'de facto annexation'. Warming toward absorption. Bond - affinity: Ossetians are kin to North Ossetia inside Russia, which is the integration argument.
